dimensions.note: No credential or secret handling. The terminal-keymap methods write per-user config bodies (pi keybindings, Ghostty config) and paths, neither of which is sensitive; no vault reference is needed and no secret is logged.

Each of the seven methods logs at info with structured placeholders and no interpolation: probed outer/platform/capability, read gsettings/xdg id, planned strategy/chords, pi keybindings written/unchanged, Ghostty config written/unchanged plus removed-binding count, xdg no-op reason or before->after id, and Ghostty verify installed/present/font-match. No secret or config-body values are logged.

Missing CLI binaries return null from run() and are recorded as unavailable rather than throwing (readDefaultTerminal, verifyGhosttyConfig). apply writes happen before writeResource, so a permission or I/O failure throws and leaves no half-written data record. The /proc ancestry walk is denied by Deno except under --allow-all; readProcAncestry now returns that as an error and probeTerminalChain records it in ancestryUnavailable and appends it to reason, instead of presenting an empty chain as fact. No broad catch swallows write errors; only Deno.env/command start and JSON.parse are guarded, each with a defined fallback.

agent_config_test.ts now runs 29 tests. Coverage: pure helpers (classifyTerminal across Ghostty/kitty/WezTerm/VTE/WSL/GNOME/unknown, planKeymapFromProbe branches, mergePiKeybindings, resolve paths, mergeGhosttyConfig idempotency/conflict-stripping, sha256Hex, path splitting), readProcAncestry shape and its unavailable path, plus method-level I/O tests for applyPiKeybindings (fresh write, idempotent re-run, preservation of unrelated keys) and applyGhosttyConfig (temp-file merge, idempotent re-run). Not unit-tested: probeTerminalChain, readDefaultTerminal, applyXdgDefaultTerminal, and verifyGhosttyConfig (they depend on the host /proc, gsettings, xdg-terminal-exec, or ghostty; the workflow is the integration path).

All apply methods are idempotent: pi keybindings merge and skip the write when the desired mapping already holds; mergeGhosttyConfig strips every font-family and conflicting ctrl+enter line and re-appends a canonical pair, so a re-run is byte-identical (asserted by test); xdg-default writes only when content differs and records changed=false otherwise. Content hashes are stored so agent-config drift detection can watch each written file.
No external HTTP or network calls. Only local CLI probes (gsettings, xdg-terminal-exec, ghostty, command -v) and local filesystem reads/writes.

Subprocesses use Deno.Command(...).output(), which drains and closes stdin/stdout/stderr on every path. No temp files or open handles are created; file reads use readTextIfPresent and return null instead of leaking errors.
README examples and tests use generic names and OS temp dirs; no real hostnames, IPs, account identifiers, or personal paths are committed. Test fixtures use /a/b, /h, and C:\Lo placeholders.

Seven strict z.object schemas (TerminalProbeSchema, XdgDefaultTerminalCurrentSchema, KeymapPlanSchema, PiKeybindingsSchema, GhosttyConfigSchema, XdgDefaultTerminalSchema, GhosttyVerifySchema); no .passthrough(), so CEL expression validation against probe/plan attributes works. This patch adds ancestryUnavailable as a nullable schema field.

Every new spec sets both fields: transient snapshots (terminalProbe, xdgDefaultTerminalCurrent, keymapPlan, ghosttyVerify) use lifetime 7d; applied-state records that drift detection must keep watching (piKeybindings, ghosttyConfig, xdgDefaultTerminal) use lifetime infinite. All use garbageCollection 10.
Not a CRUD lifecycle model. It inventories agent config and applies/idempotently reconciles terminal config; there is no create/update/delete/sync resource lifecycle to complete.

The only mutating methods (apply*) are gated by the workflow's manual_approval step and default to diagnosis-only (apply=false); they also require an explicit platform/GNOME check (xdg) or resolved path, and create missing parent dirs rather than failing. No destructive operation exists, so no skip-label policy is required.

Every data instance name is unique and written by one method: terminal-probe, xdg-default-terminal-current, keymap-plan, pi-keybindings, ghostty-config, xdg-default-terminal, ghostty-verify. xdg-default-terminal is written by the no-op and active branches of the same method with an identical schema.
Stateless methods: they read and write local files directly and use no dataRepository or stored-resource read-back.

mechanical.schema-write-conformance: pass — enumerated every writeResource against its spec. terminalProbe writes method, timestamp, term, termProgram, wslDistroName, tmuxActive, herdrPaneId, ancestry, ancestryUnavailable, plus every classification field. xdgDefaultTerminalCurrent, keymapPlan, piKeybindings, ghosttyConfig, xdgDefaultTerminal (both branches), and ghosttyVerify each populate every declared schema field with real values; no placeholder writes (the null printIdBefore/printIdAfter in the xdg no-op branch are genuinely not run, not stand-ins).
mechanical.truncation-honesty: pass — verifyGhosttyConfig caps rawOutput at 20000 chars and rawOutputTruncated records whether it was capped. readProcAncestry's max-8 walk reports ancestryUnavailable when the chain cannot be read at all.
mechanical.instance-name-consistency: pass — one writer per instance name; the two writers of xdg-default-terminal are the no-op and active branches of applyXdgDefaultTerminal, sharing XdgDefaultTerminalSchema.
mechanical.schema-field-coverage: pass — all seven schemas have a producing code path for every field, including nullable probe misses, ancestryUnavailable, and the absent-ghostty verification branch.
